description.en:
An extremely rare SF work that was never collected after serialization in Volumes 2-8 of Manga Kisou Tengai (マンガ奇想天外) in 1980-81. The manga would get collected in the Otomo Complete Works with its own volume. 

From amazon.jp:
This is a collection of works created by Katsuhiro Otomo between 1980 and 1981, when he was 26-27 years old. 

The collection includes the title work, which was serialized across six chapters in the quarterly magazine “Manga Kisotengai” published by Kisotengai-sha, as well as four short manga, a one-shot manga, and an Anthology series consisting of 12 stories. The S F work “APPLE PARADISE,” a mystery set on a huge resource-mining spaceship that is about to return to Earth from a distant planet, was never collected into tankobon form as was the case with the previous volume “G,” but now all six chapters (approx. 120 pages/unfinished) have finally been collected. 

The collection also includes the Wild West masterpiece “Memories of St. Bartholomew's Hill” and the complete “That's Amazing World” an anthology series based on fairy tales and literature. The short stories in the collection include two from “**SOS Greater Tokyo Exploration Team** (SOS Daitokyo Tankentai, SOS大東京探検隊)” (1996, Kodansha), first and fourth short stories from “**Her Thoughts...**(彼女の想いで…)” (1990, Kodansha), first and eighth short stories from “**Hansel and Gretel**” (1981, Sony Magazines), and one short story from ‘**GOOD WEATHER**’ (1981/Kitan-sha). 

The short story “I・N・R・I” was changed to the right-hand side when it was first published in a book, but in this book, it was changed back to the left-hand side as in the original manuscript and read from the end of the book, and also reprinted in nishoku as it was first published in the magazine. In addition, the short story “ELECTRIC BIRD LAND,” which appeared in black and white in the tankobon, is reproduced for the first time in its original nishoku version as it appeared in the magazine.

---
- **Volume 7 of the OTOMO COMPLETE WORKS**

biography.en:
**Name In Native Language:** 大友克洋

Ootomo Katsuhiro (born April 14, 1954) is a Japanese manga artist, screenwriter, animator, and film director. He, [Miyazaki Hayao](https://mangadex.org/author/6cdfb695-afc4-43af-bf76-20b2a4b37a7f), and [Mamoru Oshii](https://mangadex.org/author/1530ea1e-ba08-4dee-b2e6-a96b93849757) are together known as the “three giants of Japanese animation direction”.

In 1954, Otomo was born in Miyagi Prefecture. When he was young, he was deeply influenced by Tezuka's *Astro Boy* and *Jungle Emperor*, and determined to become a manga artist in middle school. In 1980, he began to serialize his famous work *Domu*, and in 1982, he began to serialize his most famous work *Akira*. In 1983, he began to participate in the production of animated films, and produced the animated film *Akira* based on his own manga in 1988, which achieved great success. Then his creative focus gradually shifted to animated films.

“A boy with extraordinary abilities stands on the ruins of Tokyo, and everyone will say that this is Katsuhiro Otomo.”
\-Miyazaki Hayao
